newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arab ministers in Cairo for Mideast peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Arab ministers in Cairo for Mideast peace talks.

text.p: Arab foreign ministers began arriving in Cairo on Friday for two days of Arab League talks on the Middle East peace process.
But the League said the ministers would not officially discuss the Iraqi crisis, which is not on their agenda.

The ministers, except for the Iraqi representative, will meet informally on Friday evening to discuss the future of peace talks between Israel and its Arab neighbours and then again on Saturday for an emergency Arab League meeting on the issue.

The ministers, which include Syria's Farouq al-Shara who arrived earlier, are also likely to discuss Damascus's refusal of an American-Israeli proposal to restart stalled peace talks with the Jewish state.
The 22-member organisation will also hold its routine six-monthly meeting, but diplomats said proposed United States airstrikes against Iraq were bound to come up.

U.S. radar-evading Stealth fighter planes were reported to have arrived in Kuwait and an aircraft carrier headed to the Gulf on Friday for widely expected attacks to punish Iraqi President Saddam Hussein for defying patrols of no-fly zones over his country.
Iraqi Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf told reporters on arrival in Cairo that Baghdad alone was reponsible for safeguarding its people and vowed to stand firm against U.S. attacks.
"The protection of Iraq is the responsibility of its people and not the responsibility of any other country," Sahaf said. "We will repulse American threats."
Asked whether Iraq would discuss the issue at the talks, Sahaf said: "I am here to take part in the regular discussion of the items on the agenda."
Libya's Unity Affairs Minister Jomaa al-Fezzani has already condemned the threatened attack.

Lebanese Foreign Minister Faris Bouez said Saturday's meeting was important because it would address changes in the Middle East peace process since hardliner Benjamin Netanyahu became Israel's prime minister in May.

"This is the first meeting after Israel's new government embarked on a media campaign to hide its anti-peace policy. Israel is trying to show that it is keen on peace while it is actually its murderer," Bouez told reporters.
Israel on Friday rocketed suspected Hizbollah bases in southern Lebanon, heightening fears that the Jewish state may launch a widescale military attack.
Sudanese Foreign Minister Ali Osman Mohammad Taha, Tunisia's Habib Ben Yahia and Farouk Kaddoumi, the head of the PLO'S political department, have also arrived.
Kuwait's Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah will also attend the Arab meetings with the foreign ministers of Algeria, the United Arab Emirates and the Comoros.
Jordan, Saudi Arabia and Oman have all sent senior foreign affairs officials while Qatar sent its transport and communications minister.
